headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection and data leakage: Plane can ingest files/links while Semantic Kernel can read/write files and use MCP/plugins, creating a shared-content pathway.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Plane ingests files, images, hyperlinks, and notes, while Semantic Kernel can read/write application-defined files and use MCP servers/plugins. That creates a plausible shared-content bridge where attacker-controlled content from Plane could be treated as instructions by Semantic Kernel. No direct provenance controls are documented, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Plane content is forwarded into Semantic Kernel prompts or plugins without provenance tagging
IF Semantic Kernel parses file or MCP content as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Add a strict instruction/data delimiter in the handoff prompt
Disable automatic ingestion of Plane attachments into agent prompts
Require allowlisted MIME types for any shared files
Log and review any MCP tool calls for prompt-like content
requires-engineering: add provenance labels end-to-end

B_data_leakage.rationale: Plane touches files, notes, issues, tasks, and roadmaps, and Semantic Kernel has broad network egress plus file read/write and plugin credentials. If both operate on the same workspace or memory store, sensitive work items can flow from Plane into Semantic Kernel outputs or third-party APIs. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default deployments, though not directly proven.
conditions: IF Plane and Semantic Kernel share a filesystem, memory store, or synced workspace
IF Semantic Kernel sends retrieved file contents to an external model provider or plugin
mitigations: Separate workspaces for the two agents
Restrict Semantic Kernel to non-sensitive projects
Turn off automatic file retrieval from shared storage
Rotate or scope plugin credentials narrowly
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before outbound calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Plane cannot write its own filesystem, but Semantic Kernel can write files and supports multiple instances with shared state via memory store. If both instances target the same mutable workspace or shared memory, they can overwrite or race on artifacts even without git access. The conflict is real but narrower than high because Plane lacks direct write capability.
conditions: IF Semantic Kernel instances share the same writable directory or memory store
IF Plane outputs are mirrored into files that Semantic Kernel also edits
mitigations: Assign separate output directories per agent
Use per-instance namespaces in the memory store
Disable concurrent writes to shared artifacts
Add file-level locking around shared outputs
requires-engineering: introduce orchestrator-level coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plane produces issues, tasks, roadmaps, files, and hyperlinks, and Semantic Kernel is a function-calling orchestrator that can act on plugin outputs. If Plane content is fed into Semantic Kernel without verification, Semantic Kernel may propagate or operationalize incorrect task data. The pathway exists in default integration patterns, but there is no evidence of fully autonomous downstream action, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Semantic Kernel uses Plane outputs as authoritative inputs
IF downstream plugins or tools execute actions based on those inputs without a verification step
mitigations: Insert a human review step before actions
Require citations or source links for every Plane-derived claim
Compare Plane outputs against a second source
Mark Plane data as untrusted in the orchestrator
requires-engineering: add validation rules before tool execution

E_compliance.rationale: Plane is self-hostable and touches work-management data, while Semantic Kernel is a library that can send context to Azure OpenAI, OpenAI, Hugging Face, or MCP servers. The main compliance risk is a residency or retention mismatch if Plane data is routed through external providers. This is not inherently a violation from the profiles alone, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF Plane data includes regulated personal or customer information
IF Semantic Kernel forwards that data to a provider or MCP server outside the required jurisdiction or retention policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared prompt
Use a self-hosted model endpoint
Review provider residency and retention settings
Minimize logged context in Semantic Kernel
requires-engineering: enforce policy-based routing
